subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for the vehicle, keeping the model static and building it with boxes, cylinders, extrusions, and glow effects while avoiding risky APIs.

Now I'm working out the truck's dimensions and layout: a roughly 7m-long frame facing +Z with a cab up front, cargo bed behind, six wheels at radius 0.62 touching the ground, and a chassis box supporting everything. I'm sketching out the cab's side profile as an extruded outline to get its angled windshield and roofline right.

Placing the windshield plane oriented along the outward normal with cyan glow, then setting up side window planes on both faces at matching offsets.

Now I'm adding the front details: a bumper box with ram spikes, a glowing headlight strip with amber lamps on each side, and a decal plane for the grille texture on the lower front face.

For the rear, I'm placing a cargo bed as an armored container with paneled paint, then topping it with either a missile launcher pod of tilted tubes or a rotating turret mounted on a ring at the back.

Now I'm adding twin cannon barrels tilted slightly upward with glowing muzzles, plus a separate rear missile rack of six angled tubes with glowing red caps positioned behind the turret. I'm also planning dark armor skirts over the wheel arches and laying out the six wheel axle positions along the body.

For the wheels, I'm sizing dark tire cylinders with glowing magenta hub rings offset outward from the body, and noting that the tires will overlap the chassis bottom slightly, so I'll add small arch cover boxes to visually mask that intersection.

I'm adding antennas and a sensor dome on the cab roof, plus decal textures like hazard stripes and an "NX-77" emblem using a simple panel-paint approach with seam lines. Then I'm placing twin exhaust stacks with glowing tips behind the cab, fuel tanks on the sides, and scattering random greeble boxes across the cargo roof and sides for detail.

Now I'm adding small glow-box side lights along the cargo rows, rear bumper and tail lights with red glow, and hatch door texturing, plus setting up a handful of SVG textures (hazard stripes, emblem, cyan HUD windshield, grille, rear door panel, side plate text) and a glow helper so textured parts emit their texture colors while dark areas stay dim. I'm also defining box and wheel helper functions to simplify building parts without needing joints.

Writing hull paint function...

Positioning the barrels so they clear the cab roof, adjusting their angle and length so they extend forward without clipping through the cabin geometry.

Now I'm adding a missile rack at the rear - a box base holding two rows of three angled tubes pointing up and forward, with glowing tips, plus underbody details like differential housings and the drive shaft near the axles.

I'm also placing a roof antenna with a glowing tip sphere, a magenta light bar on the cab roof, and side fuel tank cylinders positioned in the gap between the front and rear axles, checking the spacing carefully to avoid wheel collisions.

Now I'm adding a spiked ram bumper with cones pointing forward, a cyan-magenta neon strip along the cargo base, and side decal plates for the cargo with an emblem and "2077" text rendered via SVG.

I'm also mapping out hazard stripe planes for the rear door and bumper, positioning a rear door panel with lines and red lights at the back of the cargo box, and figuring out the connector gap between cab and cargo, plus cab side trim with door line decals and mirrored window planes.

Now I'm working out the window and door line plane sizes and offsets to avoid z-fighting, then planning a greebling pass of roughly 36 small boxes across the cargo roof using a seeded RNG, skipping zones near the turret and rack mounts.

Adding side ribs and wheel/tire geometry...

Positioning the windshield plane with its outward normal computed from the slope direction, offsetting it slightly for visibility, and sizing it to fit the cab width with a dark HUD texture.
